title: Fix macOS PowerSync stuck-state after transient 401
description: Installed Mac app authenticates + writes locally but never syncs up after transient auth('session expired') 401s (StreamingSyncClient gets stuck; only $local bucket, ps_crud ops pile up, restart doesn't recover). BackendConnector.fetchCredentials/uploadData call token.invalidate() on any 401, nuking a still-valid 30-day session. Fix: don't invalidate on transient 401s - retry credential fetch with backoff, validate/recover the session on launch, and only sign out on a confirmed-invalid session (e.g. 401 from /api/auth/token with a definitive body). Verify the installed app resumes uploading the queued ps_crud ops.
acceptance_criteria: After a transient backend blip, the Mac app re-establishes sync automatically (or on relaunch) and flushes queued ops; a valid session is never discarded on a transient 401.

title: Passwordless email-code login (magic code)
description: Login by entering email -> we email a 6-digit code -> enter code -> session issued (no password). Backend: POST /api/auth/email-code (always 200) creates a short-lived code (email_login_codes: email, code_hash, expires_at ~10min, attempts, consumed_at), emails it; POST /api/auth/email-code/verify checks code+attempts, creates the user if new (passwordless account) or signs in existing, returns opaque session token. Throttle per ip+email; cap verify attempts. UI: 'Email me a code' path on all sign-in gates with a code-entry step. Requires the mailer.
acceptance_criteria: New + existing users can sign in with just an emailed code; codes expire + are single-use; attempts capped; works on web/iOS/macOS.

title: Forgot password (email reset link/code)
description: Self-serve password reset. Add a 'Forgot password?' affordance on all sign-in gates (web, iOS, macOS). Backend: POST /api/auth/forgot starts a reset (always 200, no account enumeration); emails a short-lived single-use code/link; POST /api/auth/reset consumes the code + new password, rotates password_hash, revokes existing sessions. New password_resets table (user_id, code_hash, expires_at ~15min, consumed_at). Rate-limited per ip+email. Requires the email-sending capability (mailer).
acceptance_criteria: User can request a reset, receive an email, set a new password, and sign in with it; old sessions revoked; no account enumeration; codes single-use + expiring.

title: iOS TestFlight blocked: enable App Groups capability in Apple Developer portal

TestFlight archive fails: automatic signing can't add com.apple.security.application-groups because the capability isn't enabled on the App IDs and the group doesn't exist. The ASC API key CANNOT create App Groups (Apple limitation) — this is a one-time manual portal step.

Steps (developer.apple.com/account, team 8X4ZN58TYH):
1. Identifiers → App Groups → (+) → register 'group.dev.crmitchelmore.capture' (name e.g. 'Capture').
2. Identifiers → dev.crmitchelmore.capture.ios → edit → enable 'App Groups' capability → assign group.dev.crmitchelmore.capture.
3. Same for dev.crmitchelmore.capture.ios.share.
4. Re-run the release-ios.yml workflow (gh workflow run release-ios.yml) — automatic signing will then include the group and the archive/upload will succeed.

No code change needed; entitlements already reference the group. Alternative stopgap (not done, would regress quick-entry): ship without Share extension + App Group.
notes: Tooling plan: keep release-ios.yml/gh/xcodebuild for archive+upload. Use Webwright/Playwright browser automation only for the Apple Developer portal App Groups gap if App Store Connect API/fastlane cannot mutate the group assignment. Requires user-signed-in browser/2FA; do not store Apple password.

title: Full social login (Apple, Google, GitHub)
description: LONG-TERM BACKLOG. Federated sign-in additively layered on the existing user model via user_identities (provider, subject -> users.id). OAuth/OIDC flows per provider; link to existing email accounts; no reshaping of ownership. Apple + Google first, GitHub optional.
acceptance_criteria: Users can sign in with Apple/Google/GitHub and land on the same account as their email; identities linkable.
notes: GitHub OAuth app registered by user; client ID stored in Railway as GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID. Backend/web GitHub OAuth first step is implemented and deployed behind config gate. Button remains hidden and /start returns 503 until GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET is set directly as a secret/env var; no client secret was shared in chat.

comments.author: Chris Mitchelmore
comments.text: Blocked on provider setup rather than code structure: need Google OAuth client ID/secret + allowed redirect origins, GitHub OAuth app client ID/secret + callback URL, and Apple Services ID/web domain + Apple/native entitlement decision after the prior Developer ID SIWA signing issue. Implementation should be additive on existing user_identities and must route first-factor social sessions through issueSessionOrMfa so TOTP/recovery remains enforced.
